decisions.text: Design the remote control to be sleek, simple, and with a limited number of buttons.
Include all proposed features initially and refine them later in the process.

notes:
## Remote Control Functionality
- The device must turn the TV on and off immediately upon pressing the big button, with no delay or 'waffling'.
- Remote controls should be easy to find and not easily lost.
- The remote should provide an oral cue to confirm when the command has been received.
## Design and Material Preferences
- The remote should be waterproof to handle spills or outdoor use.
- The remote should be unbreakable to withstand drops and play by children.
- The remote should be inflatable and change size based on user preference.
- Titanium was suggested as a material option, though concerns were raised about its weight and cost.
## Project Goals and Pricing
- The company aims to make at least 50 million Euro; the price must be reasonable on the sales side.
- Marketing Expert suggests a sales price of 25 Euro with a production price of 12.5 Euro, noting this is a market price for 15-35 year-olds willing to spend on trendy items.
- Management wants a totally new product that could cost more but create a boom in the market.
## Remote Control Design
- The remote control should be slim (not fat) and universal for any TV.
- Marketing Expert suggests adding color to make it trendy and fancy.
- Design should be sleek and simple, minimizing the number of buttons to avoid clutter and confusion.
- Frequently used buttons (power, channel, volume) should be larger and strategically placed.
- Existing remotes often have too many buttons, tiny labels, and complex sequences that users forget.
## Speech Recognition Feature
- 80% of 15-35 year-olds are willing to spend more for trendy items; 75-90% are willing to pay for speech recognition on a remote.
- Proposal: Single-word recognition commands (e.g., 'remote', 'on', 'off') with a beep sound to help users find the device among clutter.
- Challenge: Speech recognition must filter out ambient TV sound and user speech to avoid false triggers (e.g., turning off TV when a movie character speaks).
- Proposal: Use exact single-word recognition similar to telephone or car systems.
- Project Manager offered to recommend technical partners like Intel or IBM for speech recognition training and technical backup.
## Power and Battery
- Speech recognition and fancy features may impact battery life.
- Proposal: Add wireless charging or a solar cell inside the remote.
## Feature Selection Strategy
- The team agreed to include all proposed features initially and eliminate them later in the process.
- User Interface Designer suggested starting with all features might waste time on features that will be discarded.
## Next Steps
- Project Manager will send meeting minutes and help coordinate with technical companies for design support.
- Team will take a lunch break and reconvene in the next meeting to discuss further.
tldr: The team discussed functional design requirements for a new remote control, including instant on/off functionality, durability, and user-friendly features. They debated material options, project goals, and speech recognition features before agreeing on a sleek design and a strategy to include all proposed features initially.
